data.current_summary: Fetch a single normalized record by recordId or uuid
data.current_description:
Resolves a record by EITHER identifier a search published for it: our `recordId` (`rec_…`) or the registry's own `uuid`. DATABASE-BACKED since 2026-08-04 — it previously read only an in-memory index local to one API container, keyed on `recordId` alone, so a `uuid` never resolved and a `recordId` resolved only when the follow-up request happened to reach the same container as the search.

A `404` means THIS IDENTIFIER IS NOT CURRENT — never that the person is unregistered. Registries re-issue their ids (KY, MO, OR, AZ, IA and WV each re-issued their entire registry within eight days to 2026-08-04; CA re-issued ~104,000). Re-search by name and state, then store the new `uuid`.

An identifier carrying a byte no id of ours can hold — a NUL or any other control character — is also a `404`. Until 2026-08-05 `/v1/records/%00` and `/v1/records/a%00b` returned **500**, the only 5xx reachable from ~60 hostile inputs, because the NUL reached a database parameter. A 5xx is a claim that WE failed, and for a malformed id that claim is false. `%01` and `%25` always answered 404; now every impossible id answers the same way.

A `409` means the id is AMBIGUOUS. A `uuid` is unique only together with its jurisdiction — `20059` identifies a Florida, a Pennsylvania and a Wisconsin registrant, and 55,893 ids are shared across jurisdictions (147,624 records). This endpoint returns one record and will not guess which you meant; use `GET /v1/compat/sexoffender?uuid=…&state=XX`, which returns every match with its jurisdiction, or use `recordId`, which is namespaced per jurisdiction and does not collide.

**Important:** A 404 indicates the identifier is no longer current (registries re-issue ids periodically), not that the person is unregistered. A 409 indicates the uuid is ambiguous across jurisdictions; use recordId (which is jurisdiction-namespaced) or the compat endpoint with state parameter to disambiguate. Malformed identifiers (containing control characters) also return 404.

A `200` means the message is **recorded**: it is stored against the `submissionId` in the response and can be looked up by that id if you ever need to refer to it. It does not report that an email has arrived anywhere, because that is a separate step we do not make you wait for.

Replies come from the address in `supportEmail`, normally within one business day. You can also write to that address directly; both routes reach the same inbox.

The endpoint accepts `application/json` or `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`, so an ordinary HTML form can post to it without any JavaScript.

Accepts both `application/json` and `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` content types.

data.current_summary: offenders.io drop-in compatibility (POST)
data.current_description:
Accepts offenders.io's exact parameters and returns their exact envelope ({offenders, page, totalPages[, error]}). Existing offenders.io integrations switch by changing only the base URL and key. Accepts the key via `X-API-Key`, `Authorization: Bearer`, or `?key=`. Echoes/mints the offenders.io correlation headers (`X-Request-Id`, `X-Offenders-Request-Id`, `X-Offendersearch-Request-Id`). Errors use the offenders.io `{code, message}` shape.

**Combination-validation (400 with `{code:400, message}`):** `q` cannot be combined with `firstName`/`lastName`, nor with `lat`/`lng`; `address` cannot be combined with `q`, nor with `lat`/`lng`.

**GIS search (`lat`+`lng` supplied):** results are paged **50 per page** (regular searches page 20), and the query defaults to the **last 90 days** of source updates (`updatedAtStart = now − 90d`) unless the caller supplies an explicit `updatedAtStart`. A missing `radius` defaults to 1 mile (capped at 100).

Preserves offenders.io correlation headers (X-Request-Id, X-Offenders-Request-Id, X-Offendersearch-Request-Id) and error format ({code, message}).

**Parameter constraints:** `q` cannot be combined with `firstName`/`lastName` or `lat`/`lng`; `address` cannot be combined with `q` or `lat`/`lng`.

**Geographic search:** When `lat` and `lng` are supplied, results page at 50 per page (vs. 20 for name searches), default to last 90 days of updates, and `radius` defaults to 1 mile (max 100 miles).

Resolves a record by EITHER identifier a search published for it: our `recordId` (`rec_…`) or the registry's own `uuid`. DATABASE-BACKED since 2026-08-04 — it previously read only an in-memory index local to one API container, keyed on `recordId` alone, so a `uuid` never resolved and a `recordId` resolved only when the follow-up request happened to reach the same container as the search.

A `404` means THIS IDENTIFIER IS NOT CURRENT — never that the person is unregistered. Registries re-issue their ids (KY, MO, OR, AZ, IA and WV each re-issued their entire registry within eight days to 2026-08-04; CA re-issued ~104,000). Re-search by name and state, then store the new `uuid`.

An identifier carrying a byte no id of ours can hold — a NUL or any other control character — is also a `404`. Until 2026-08-05 `/v1/records/%00` and `/v1/records/a%00b` returned **500**, the only 5xx reachable from ~60 hostile inputs, because the NUL reached a database parameter. A 5xx is a claim that WE failed, and for a malformed id that claim is false. `%01` and `%25` always answered 404; now every impossible id answers the same way.

A `409` means the id is AMBIGUOUS. A `uuid` is unique only together with its jurisdiction — `20059` identifies a Florida, a Pennsylvania and a Wisconsin registrant, and 55,893 ids are shared across jurisdictions (147,624 records). This endpoint returns one record and will not guess which you meant; use `GET /v1/compat/sexoffender?uuid=…&state=XX`, which returns every match with its jurisdiction, or use `recordId`, which is namespaced per jurisdiction and does not collide.
data.summary_suggestion: Retrieve a single offender record by recordId or uuid
data.description_suggestion:
Retrieves a normalized offender record by either our internal `recordId` (rec_…) or the registry's `uuid`. Returns a Record object containing all offender information.

**Important:** A 404 indicates the identifier is no longer current (registries re-issue ids periodically), not that the person is unregistered. A 409 indicates the uuid is ambiguous across jurisdictions; use recordId (which is jurisdiction-namespaced) or the compat endpoint with state parameter to disambiguate. Malformed identifiers (containing control characters) also return 404.

data.current_summary: Search US criminal records — jail, prison, court and warrant
data.current_description:
Searches county jail booking rosters, statewide prison systems, court sources and warrant systems across more than a thousand county, state and federal jurisdictions.

☠ `lastName` is REQUIRED. An unbounded criminal query is refused rather than answered from an arbitrary slice that would differ run to run — a name is the field that cannot be enumerated. Supply `firstName` and a `dob` or `birthYear` wherever you have them; a bare common surname matches thousands of people and the score cannot tell you which is yours.

☠ READ `recordType` BEFORE CHARACTERISING ANYONE. A jail booking is an ARREST-stage record — charges at booking are frequently reduced, dismissed or never filed, and it is not a conviction. Prison custody implies a sentence. A court record carries the disposition, which is the authoritative statement of how a case ended. A warrant means the person is sought and nothing has been tested.

Not a consumer report — not for FCRA-covered decisions.

data.current_summary: Send a message to the Offendersearch team
data.current_description:
Sends a message to our support team. **No API key required** — this is the endpoint behind the contact form on offendersearch.app, and it is open because the people who need it most are the ones who do not have a key yet.

A `200` means the message is **recorded**: it is stored against the `submissionId` in the response and can be looked up by that id if you ever need to refer to it. It does not report that an email has arrived anywhere, because that is a separate step we do not make you wait for.

Replies come from the address in `supportEmail`, normally within one business day. You can also write to that address directly; both routes reach the same inbox.

The endpoint accepts `application/json` or `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`, so an ordinary HTML form can post to it without any JavaScript.

data.current_summary: offenders.io drop-in compatibility (POST)
data.current_description:
Accepts offenders.io's exact parameters and returns their exact envelope ({offenders, page, totalPages[, error]}). Existing offenders.io integrations switch by changing only the base URL and key. Accepts the key via `X-API-Key`, `Authorization: Bearer`, or `?key=`. Echoes/mints the offenders.io correlation headers (`X-Request-Id`, `X-Offenders-Request-Id`, `X-Offendersearch-Request-Id`). Errors use the offenders.io `{code, message}` shape.

**Combination-validation (400 with `{code:400, message}`):** `q` cannot be combined with `firstName`/`lastName`, nor with `lat`/`lng`; `address` cannot be combined with `q`, nor with `lat`/`lng`.

**GIS search (`lat`+`lng` supplied):** results are paged **50 per page** (regular searches page 20), and the query defaults to the **last 90 days** of source updates (`updatedAtStart = now − 90d`) unless the caller supplies an explicit `updatedAtStart`. A missing `radius` defaults to 1 mile (capped at 100).
